headline: Panthers' Brad Marchand could be back in 6 weeks after knee injury
take:
ESPN reports that Brad Marchand could return in about six weeks after a knee injury, with the Panthers forward saying Thursday he's glad it wasn't more serious as he rehabs.

His 2 games this season are too few to read much into, but the signs were good: FLA controlled 65 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) while he played, and the team's share was about 12 percentage points better with him on the ice. He did that in 11:23 a night on the third line and second power-play unit, and he scored 27 goals and 54 points in 52 games last year. FLA sits at 9-5-2 and creates slightly more quality chances than it allows (53.6 percent), so the team can absorb the absence, though it loses a proven scorer.

The Panthers have already played 5 games without him, and the shifts are visible. Carter Verhaeghe has taken his spot beside Reinhart and Tkachuk, Lars Eller is up to 16:58 a night from 12:14, and Garnet Hathaway is up to 10:14 from 8:41. Those are the players to watch for added ice time while Marchand is out.
